assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's 2001-2003 proposal of magic-wavelength trapping in an optical lattice removed Doppler and recoil shifts together with light-shift errors, and Ye's group turned it into clocks at the 1e-18 level. The result is a clean, original invention that redefined the limit of precision measurement, with uses in relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and the planned redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the originating idea; Ye led the decisive demonstration of ultrahigh accuracy and the frequency-comb and ultrastable-laser infrastructure. A two-person prize is natural and the credited list supports it. Ye's frequency-comb work built on the 2005 prize to Hall and Hänsch, which does not itself pre-empt the lattice-clock invention, though some would want clock pioneers beyond these two (for example Ludlow, Hinkley) to be considered.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across Tokyo, JILA, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others is extensive, with agreement at the 1e-18 level and stable interpretation. Timing is ripe because the second redefinition discussion is active.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to weight the contribution of the ion-clock tradition (Wineland, already recognised in 2012) against the lattice-clock invention.
Credit for the ultrastable cavity-stabilised lasers underlying the best results is distributed beyond the credited pair.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 trapped-ion quantum gate proposal and the subsequent neutral-atom, Rydberg and optical-lattice proposals created the conceptual toolbox for quantum computing and simulation in atomic systems. The work is original, concrete and implementable, and it has shaped the experimental programmes of several Nobel-recognised and Nobel-adjacent groups.
assessment.attribution: The pairing of Cirac and Zoller is the standard and well-defined attribution for the ion-trap gate and the lattice-simulation proposals, so the two-name configuration is fair. The experimental realisation belongs to other groups (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe, Bloch and others), which is outside this candidate's scope but narrows the credit to a theory prize.
assessment.maturity: The proposals have been realised experimentally in many platforms over three decades, so the predictions are strongly confirmed. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: A theory-only prize may be seen as awkward given that Wineland was honoured in 2012 for ion control.
Overlap with B008 and B009, which also credit Zoller, could split support across candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene and the Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant insulators, followed by the observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened the field of topological materials. The idea is original, general and of lasting consequence across condensed matter, photonics and cold atoms.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the Hasan and Moore-Balents and Fu contributions, are not within this entry's credited names, so the allocation remains contested and a three-name list is only one of several defensible choices.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation in HgTe and then three-dimensional systems is robust and independent. The field is mature and the recognition is timely, though the 2016 prize already honoured topological phase transitions.
uncertainties: Disputed priority among Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Moore-Balents, Fu-Kane-Mele and Roy, only partly reflected in the credited names.
Relationship to the 2016 topological phases prize may be judged by others as partial overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of a flat band at the magic angle and the observation of correlated insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the whole field of moire quantum matter. The discovery is surprising and has an enormous follow-on literature.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 band-structure prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulation and superconductivity. The pairing of theory and experiment gives a logical configuration, but Cao, Fatemi and others from the experimental team are outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the phases, but the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not fully stable. Recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity remains unsettled.
Experimental credit within the Jarillo-Herrero team and the role of Dean's group and others in related platforms are not fully captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realising the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and Fermi-Hubbard physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including single-site quantum gas microscopy, gave controllable quantum simulators of strongly correlated matter. The work is deeply connected to atomic physics and has changed how many-body models are tested.
assessment.attribution: The Mott transition experiment came from Greiner, Bloch and collaborators in Hansch's group, with Jaksch-Zoller theory behind it; Esslinger led fermionic lattice work and Greiner the microscope. Because Zoller is also credited here and in other entries, the strongest three-experimenter configuration excludes him; Hansch's role and Jaksch are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Quantum simulation is established in a variety of laboratories, though the scientific payoff beyond benchmarking is still developing, so maturity is good but not complete.
uncertainties: Whether the simulator payoff on open problems such as high-Tc superconductivity is sufficient yet.
Theory credit (Jaksch, Zoller) versus experimental credit cannot be balanced within three names drawn from this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BB84 protocol turned the no-cloning properties of quantum states into secure key distribution, and it created the field of quantum cryptography. The idea is original, simple and has led to commercial systems and satellite demonstrations.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the unambiguous originators of BB84; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is an independent and conceptually distinct contribution. A two-name prize is the cleanest, and a three-name prize would be defensible, but the Ekert allocation remains debated.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation through fibre and satellite links is solid, although practical security against side-channel attacks is still an engineering matter. The 2022 prize on entanglement experiments partly overlaps with the Ekert strand.
uncertainties: Whether Ekert's protocol should be recognised alongside BB84.
Overlap with the 2022 Bell-inequality prize in the committee's eyes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms became a precision instrument for gravimetry, gravity gradients, the fine-structure constant and tests of the equivalence principle. The core ideas of light-pulse interferometers are important, original and tied to the physics of laser cooling already honoured in 1997.
assessment.attribution: Bordé developed the theoretical framework, Pritchard demonstrated early atom interferometry, and Kasevich with Chu realised light-pulse gravimeters and gradiometers. Chu's omission here is notable because he already holds the 1997 prize, which complicates the attribution; the three listed names fit a balanced prize but others (Chu, Rasel, Cronin) are not available.
assessment.maturity: Instruments are field-deployed and confirmed by several groups, and applications keep maturing. Timing is plausible rather than urgent.
uncertainties: Precedence and relative weight among Bordé, Pritchard, Kasevich and Chu.
Whether the discovery is seen as a technology extension of earlier laser-cooling recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2013 detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened neutrino astronomy and was followed by evidence for TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. It is a decisive observational discovery with a large and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the conception and construction of the instrument; Karle and Spiering are leading collaboration figures. IceCube is a collaboration of hundreds, so the prize configuration is awkward and the credited names may not capture all decisive contributors (for example the AMANDA and early DUMAND pioneers).
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly confirmed, including by other detectors, though source identification is still partial, so interpretation is still evolving.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and allocation to individuals are unresolved.
Source identification of the neutrino flux remains incomplete.
